fr: Il faut que nous soyons à l'aéroport avant sept heures du matin.
en: We must be at the airport before seven in the morning.
ipa: il fo kə nu swa.jɔ̃ a l‿a.e.ʁɔ.pɔʁ a.vɑ̃ sɛ.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The subjunctive form soyons is easy to misspell or confuse with the indicative sommes, so listen for the -oy- spelling.

fr: Le rendez-vous est prévu pour le vingt et un mars à quatorze heures trente.
en: The appointment is scheduled for March twenty-first at two thirty in the afternoon.
ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu ɛ pʁe.vy puʁ lə vɛ̃.t‿e œ̃ maʁs a ka.tɔʁ.zœʁ tʁɑ̃t
notes: The liaison in vingt et un pronounces the normally silent t of vingt before et.

fr: Nous nous verrons dans deux semaines, le temps que tu finisses ton rapport.
en: We will see each other in two weeks, by the time you finish your report.
ipa: nu nu vɛ.ʁɔ̃ dɑ̃ dø sə.mɛn lə tɑ̃ kə ty fi.nis tɔ̃ ʁa.pɔʁ
notes: The subjunctive finisses ends in a silent -es that is easy to drop when writing from dictation.

fr: C'est à neuf heures précises que la réunion commence.
en: It is at nine o'clock sharp that the meeting begins.
ipa: sɛ.t‿a nœ.vœʁ pʁe.siz kə la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ kɔ.mɑ̃s
notes: Do not confuse c'est with ces or ses; only the elided form c'est fits this sentence.

fr: Ces dates ne conviennent à personne, il faudra les changer.
en: These dates do not suit anyone, they will have to be changed.
ipa: se dat nə kɔ̃.vjɛn a pɛʁ.sɔn il fo.dʁa le ʃɑ̃.ʒe
notes: The demonstrative ces sounds identical to ses and c'est, so context alone decides the spelling.

fr: Quelle heure est-il exactement quand le train part de la gare ?
en: What time is it exactly when the train leaves the station?
ipa: kɛ.lœʁ ɛ.til ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ kɑ̃ lə tʁɛ̃ paʁ də la ɡaʁ
notes: Quelle carries a silent final e that only surfaces through the liaison with heure, unlike the masculine quel.

fr: Il y a trois ans, nous avons déménagé à Lyon au mois de juin.
en: Three years ago, we moved to Lyon in the month of June.
ipa: il i a tʁwa.z‿ɑ̃ nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ de.me.na.ʒe a ljɔ̃ o mwa də ʒɥɛ̃
notes: The liaison between trois and ans produces a z sound that must not be written into the word ans itself.

fr: Le magasin ferme ses portes à dix-huit heures trente les jours de semaine.
en: The store closes its doors at six thirty in the evening on weekdays.
ipa: lə ma.ga.zɛ̃ fɛʁm se pɔʁt a di.zɥi.tœʁ tʁɑ̃t le ʒuʁ də sə.mɛn
notes: Ses here is the possessive adjective and sounds exactly like ces and c'est, so spelling depends on meaning.

fr: D'ici la fin du mois, il faut que le projet soit terminé.
en: By the end of the month, the project needs to be finished.
ipa: di.si la fɛ̃ dy mwa il fo kə lə pʁɔ.ʒɛ swa tɛʁ.mi.ne
notes: The subjunctive soit is a homophone of soi and soie, so only the verbal context confirms the spelling.

fr: Se lever à cinq heures du matin devient difficile en hiver.
en: Getting up at five in the morning becomes difficult in winter.
ipa: sə lə.ve a sɛ̃.kœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃ də.vjɛ̃ di.fi.sil ɑ̃.n‿i.vɛʁ
notes: The reflexive pronoun se before a verb is often confused in dictation with the conjunction ce.

fr: Ses horaires de travail changent chaque semaine selon le planning.
en: Her work hours change every week depending on the schedule.
ipa: se.z‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ də tʁa.vaj ʃɑ̃ʒ ʃak sə.mɛn sə.lɔ̃ lə pla.niŋ
notes: The possessive ses liaises with the following vowel of horaires, producing a z sound that signals the plural.

fr: Bien qu'il soit déjà minuit, elle continue de travailler sur son mémoire.
en: Even though it is already midnight, she continues working on her thesis.
ipa: bjɛ̃ kil swa de.ʒa mi.nɥi ɛl kɔ̃.ti.ny də tʁa.va.je syʁ sɔ̃ me.mwaʁ
notes: After bien que, the verb must take the subjunctive soit, not the indicative est.

fr: Le concert commence à vingt heures, mais les portes ouvrent une heure avant.
en: The concert starts at eight in the evening, but the doors open an hour before.
ipa: lə kɔ̃.sɛʁ kɔ.mɑ̃s a vɛ̃.tœʁ mɛ le pɔʁt uvʁ yn œʁ a.vɑ̃
notes: The t of vingt is silent alone but resurfaces in liaison before heures, unlike in vingt et un.

fr: Nous attendons depuis longtemps que la date soit enfin fixée.
en: We have been waiting a long time for the date to finally be set.
ipa: nu.z‿a.tɑ̃.dɔ̃ də.pɥi lɔ̃.tɑ̃ kə la dat swa ɑ̃.fɛ̃ fik.se
notes: The past participle fixée takes a silent final e to agree with the feminine noun date.

fr: L'examen aura lieu le premier juillet, à huit heures du matin.
en: The exam will take place on the first of July, at eight in the morning.
ipa: lɛg.za.mɛ̃ o.ʁa ljø lə pʁə.mje ʒɥi.jɛ a ɥi.tœʁ dy ma.tɛ̃
notes: The h of huit is mute, so the liaison with the article and with heures passes right through it.

fr: Il est essentiel que vous arriviez à l'heure pour l'entretien.
en: It is essential that you arrive on time for the interview.
ipa: i.l‿ɛ.t‿e.sɑ̃.sjɛl kə vu.z‿a.ʁi.vje a lœʁ puʁ lɑ̃.tʁə.tjɛ̃
notes: The subjunctive ending -iez of arriviez is easy to mishear as the simple present -ez, so listen for the extra i.

fr: Ce mois-ci, plusieurs échéances tombent le même jour.
en: This month, several deadlines fall on the same day.
ipa: sə mwa.si ply.zjœʁ e.ʃe.ɑ̃s tɔ̃b lə mɛm ʒuʁ
notes: The demonstrative ce before mois is a homophone of se and must not be confused with the reflexive pronoun.

fr: La conférence a duré environ deux heures et demie.
en: The conference lasted about two and a half hours.
ipa: la kɔ̃.fe.ʁɑ̃s a dy.ʁe ɑ̃.vi.ʁɔ̃ dø.z‿œʁ e də.mi
notes: Demie agrees in gender with the feminine heures and keeps its final e, unlike the invariable demi placed before a noun.

fr: Depuis dix ans, cette entreprise organise son bilan chaque décembre.
en: For ten years, this company has organized its report every December.
ipa: də.pɥi di.z‿ɑ̃ sɛ.t‿ɑ̃.tʁə.pʁiz ɔʁ.ga.niz sɔ̃ bi.lɑ̃ ʃak de.sɑ̃bʁ
notes: The liaison turns the silent x of dix into a z sound before the vowel of ans.

fr: Il faudrait que nous partions avant l'aube pour éviter les embouteillages.
en: We would need to leave before dawn to avoid the traffic jams.
ipa: il fo.dʁɛ kə nu paʁ.tjɔ̃ a.vɑ̃ lob puʁ e.vi.te le.z‿ɑ̃.bu.tɛ.jaʒ
notes: The subjunctive partions is written like the imperfect partions too, so only il faudrait que confirms the mood.

fr: Le train de neuf heures a été annulé à cause du mauvais temps.
en: The nine o'clock train was cancelled because of the bad weather.
ipa: lə tʁɛ̃ də nœ.vœʁ a e.te a.ny.le a koz dy mɔ.vɛ tɑ̃
notes: The f of neuf becomes a v sound in liaison before heures, an irregular liaison worth listening for.

fr: Les vacances commencent dans une semaine exactement.
en: The holidays start in exactly one week.
ipa: le va.kɑ̃s kɔ.mɑ̃s dɑ̃.z‿yn sə.mɛn ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃
notes: The nasal ɑ̃ sound is spelled an in vacances but en in commencent, so spelling cannot rely on sound alone.

fr: C'est le vingt-cinq décembre que toute la famille se réunit.
en: It is on the twenty-fifth of December that the whole family gets together.
ipa: sɛ lə vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k de.sɑ̃bʁ kə tut la fa.mij sə ʁe.y.ni
notes: C'est is the elided form here and cannot be replaced by ces, even though both sound identical.

fr: Nous devons rendre ce dossier avant la fin de la journée.
en: We must hand in this file before the end of the day.
ipa: nu də.vɔ̃ ʁɑ̃dʁ sə dɔ.sje a.vɑ̃ la fɛ̃ də la ʒuʁ.ne
notes: The demonstrative ce before a consonant keeps its e mute, unlike cet used before a vowel.

fr: Elle est née un vendredi treize, un jour qu'elle n'oubliera jamais.
en: She was born on a Friday the thirteenth, a day she will never forget.
ipa: ɛl ɛ ne œ̃ vɑ̃.dʁə.di tʁɛz œ̃ ʒuʁ kɛl nu.bli.ʁa ʒa.mɛ
notes: The past participle née agrees in gender with the feminine subject elle and needs the silent final e.

fr: Il se peut que la livraison arrive avec plusieurs jours de retard.
en: It is possible that the delivery arrives several days late.
ipa: il sə pø kə la li.vʁɛ.zɔ̃ a.ʁiv a.vɛk ply.zjœʁ ʒuʁ də ʁə.taʁ
notes: After il se peut que, the verb stays in the subjunctive arrive, so only the trigger phrase confirms the mood.

fr: Le musée reste ouvert jusqu'à vingt-deux heures le vendredi soir.
en: The museum stays open until ten in the evening on Friday.
ipa: lə my.ze ʁɛst u.vɛʁ ʒys.ka vɛ̃t.dø.z‿œʁ lə vɑ̃.dʁə.di swaʁ
notes: The liaison between deux and heures adds a z sound not present when deux stands alone.

fr: Ces horaires d'ouverture ont changé depuis la rentrée.
en: These opening hours have changed since the start of the school year.
ipa: se.z‿ɔ.ʁɛʁ du.vɛʁ.tyʁ ɔ̃ ʃɑ̃.ʒe də.pɥi la ʁɑ̃.tʁe
notes: Ces before a vowel liaises into a z sound and should not be mistaken for the singular cet.

fr: Il a fallu attendre près d'une heure avant que le médecin nous reçoive.
en: We had to wait nearly an hour before the doctor saw us.
ipa: i.l‿a fa.ly a.tɑ̃dʁ pʁɛ dyn œʁ a.vɑ̃ kə lə med.sɛ̃ nu ʁə.swav
notes: Reçoive keeps the cedilla under the c so the sound stays soft before the vowel o, a spelling tested in dictation.

fr: Le rendez-vous fixé pour mardi a finalement été reporté à jeudi.
en: The appointment set for Tuesday was finally postponed to Thursday.
ipa: lə ʁɑ̃.de.vu fik.se puʁ maʁ.di a fi.nal.mɑ̃ e.te ʁə.pɔʁ.te a ʒø.di
notes: The past participle fixé agrees with the masculine rendez-vous and takes no extra e, unlike fixée used elsewhere.

fr: Nous partirons dès que l'horloge sonnera midi.
en: We will leave as soon as the clock strikes noon.
ipa: nu paʁ.ti.ʁɔ̃ dɛ kə lɔʁ.lɔʒ sɔn.ʁa mi.di
notes: The silent h of horloge allows the elision of the article into l'horloge, unlike words with an aspirate h.

fr: La date limite d'inscription est fixée au trente novembre.
en: The registration deadline is set for November thirtieth.
ipa: la dat li.mit dɛ̃s.kʁip.sjɔ̃ ɛ fik.se o tʁɑ̃t nɔ.vɑ̃bʁ
notes: The nasal vowel before b takes the spelling m, not n, as in novembre, a common nasal spelling rule.

fr: Il y a exactement un mois que nous avons signé ce contrat.
en: It has been exactly one month since we signed this contract.
ipa: il i a ɛg.zak.tə.mɑ̃ œ̃ mwa kə nu.z‿a.vɔ̃ si.ɲe sə kɔ̃.tʁa
notes: The demonstrative ce before contrat is a homophone of se but functions here as an adjective, not a pronoun.

fr: Quelles que soient les circonstances, la réunion aura lieu à l'heure prévue.
en: Whatever the circumstances, the meeting will take place on time.
ipa: kɛl kə swat le siʁ.kɔ̃s.tɑ̃s la ʁe.y.njɔ̃ o.ʁa ljø a lœʁ pʁe.vy
notes: Quelles que soient requires the plural feminine subjunctive, agreeing with les circonstances even though soient sounds like soit.

fr: Le film commence à vingt et une heures quinze précises.
en: The film starts at nine fifteen in the evening sharp.
ipa: lə film kɔ.mɑ̃s a vɛ̃.t‿e yn œʁ kɛ̃z pʁe.siz
notes: Une agrees with the feminine heures even inside the compound number vingt et une, unlike the masculine un used elsewhere.

fr: Nous nous sommes rencontrés il y a huit ans, presque jour pour jour.
en: We met eight years ago, almost to the day.
ipa: nu nu sɔm ʁɑ̃.kɔ̃.tʁe il i a ɥi.t‿ɑ̃ pʁɛs.kə ʒuʁ puʁ ʒuʁ
notes: The reflexive past participle rencontrés agrees with the plural subject nous and takes the final s.

fr: Bien que l'horaire soit serré, tout le monde est arrivé à temps.
en: Even though the schedule is tight, everyone arrived on time.
ipa: bjɛ̃ kə lɔ.ʁɛʁ swa se.ʁe tu lə mɔ̃d ɛ.t‿a.ʁi.ve a tɑ̃
notes: After bien que, soit is the required subjunctive and should not be replaced by the indicative est.

fr: Le décalage horaire rend les appels difficiles à organiser.
en: The time difference makes calls difficult to organize.
ipa: lə de.ka.laʒ ɔ.ʁɛʁ ʁɑ̃ le.z‿a.pɛl di.fi.sil a ɔʁ.ga.ni.ze
notes: The verb form rend ends in a silent d, easy to drop or confuse with the plural rendent where the d is pronounced.

fr: Il conviendrait que la séance soit reportée au lendemain, faute de quorum suffisant.
en: The session should be postponed to the next day, for lack of sufficient quorum.
ipa: il kɔ̃.vjɛ̃.dʁɛ kə la se.ɑ̃s swa ʁə.pɔʁ.te o lɑ̃.də.mɛ̃ fot də kɔ.ʁɔm sy.fi.zɑ̃
notes: The past participle reportée agrees in gender with the feminine séance, adding a silent final e.

fr: Nous vous serions reconnaissants de bien vouloir confirmer votre présence avant le quinze du mois courant.
en: We would be grateful if you could confirm your attendance before the fifteenth of this month.
ipa: nu vu sə.ʁjɔ̃ ʁə.kɔ.nɛ.sɑ̃ də bjɛ̃ vu.lwaʁ kɔ̃.fiʁ.me vɔtʁ pʁe.zɑ̃s a.vɑ̃ lə kɛ̃z dy mwa ku.ʁɑ̃
notes: The conditional serions ends in the silent -ions typical of formal correspondence, easy to shorten by mistake.

fr: Quoi qu'il en soit, l'échéance du trente et un décembre demeure incontournable.
en: Be that as it may, the deadline of December thirty-first remains unavoidable.
ipa: kwa kil ɑ̃ swa le.ʃe.ɑ̃s dy tʁɑ̃.t‿e œ̃ de.sɑ̃bʁ də.mœʁ ɛ̃.kɔ̃.tuʁ.nabl
notes: The fixed expression quoi qu'il en soit uses the elided qu'il, not the separate words qui il, a common dictation trap.

fr: Le communiqué, daté du vingt-deux avril deux mille vingt-cinq, précise les nouvelles modalités.
en: The statement, dated April twenty-second, two thousand twenty-five, specifies the new terms.
ipa: lə kɔ.my.ni.ke da.te dy vɛ̃t.dø a.vʁil dø mil vɛ̃t.sɛ̃k pʁe.siz le nu.vɛl mɔ.da.li.te
notes: Formal French dates write the year as deux mille vingt-cinq without a hyphen between deux and mille, unlike the compound numbers around it.

fr: Il n'est pas exclu que la cérémonie soit avancée d'une heure en cas d'intempéries.
en: It is not ruled out that the ceremony will be moved an hour earlier in case of bad weather.
ipa: il nɛ pa.z‿ɛks.kly kə la se.ʁe.mɔ.ni swa.t‿a.vɑ̃.se dyn œʁ ɑ̃ ka dɛ̃.tɑ̃.pe.ʁi
notes: The past participle avancée takes a silent final e to agree with the feminine cérémonie, unaffected by the intervening subjunctive verb.

fr: Depuis que cet accord a été signé, plus d'une décennie s'est écoulée sans révision.
en: Since this agreement was signed, more than a decade has passed without revision.
ipa: də.pɥi kə sɛ.t‿a.kɔʁ a e.te si.ɲe ply.z‿dyn de.sɛ.ni sɛ.t‿e.ku.le sɑ̃ ʁe.vi.zjɔ̃
notes: Cet replaces the standard masculine ce before the vowel-initial accord, a euphonic form chosen to allow liaison.
